hmin=

First, we recall the following definitions: * The global minimum of a function is the smallest value that the function attains on its domain. There can only be (at most) one global minimum. * A global minimum point of a function is a point (x,y) where a function reaches a global minimum. There can be zero, one, or many global minimum points. For our function, the minimum value reached by the function is h(x)=−2.
Therefore, the global minimum is hmin=−2. The function reaches this value when x=1, so the global minimum point is (1,−2).
